exercises.name: Single Arm Triceps Pushdown (Cable)

source_english.description: Stand at the high pulley and press one handle down beside the ribs by extending the elbow, then switch arms.
instructions: Stand facing a cable machine with a straight bar attachment at chest height.
Grasp the bar with an overhand grip and step back to create tension in the cable.
Position your feet shoulder-width apart and slightly bend your knees.
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Start with your arm fully extended and perpendicular to the floor.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, exhale and push the bar down until your arm is fully extended.
common_mistakes: Using momentum instead of the target joint path.
source_english.safety_note: Use a secure setup and stop if alignment or control is lost.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Press (Machine)

source_english.description: Decline Bench Press (Machine) is a supported chest press using the barbell.
instructions: Lie on a declined bench with feet secured. Grip the barbell and hold it over the chest.
Lower the resistance toward the chest with elbows controlled.
Pause without bouncing or losing shoulder position.
Press back to straight arms, then rerack or set the weights down safely.
source_english.safety_note: Use a spotter or safeties for the loaded press and stop before shoulder control is lost.

exercises.name: Chest Dip (Assisted)

source_english.description: The Chest Dip (Assisted) lowers the body by bending the elbows between parallel supports, then presses back up while the shoulders remain controlled.
instructions: Mount the parallel handles with arms straight and the torso slightly inclined.
Bend the elbows to lower until the upper arms approach parallel with the floor.
Pause before the shoulders lose control.
Press through the handles to straighten the elbows and reset.
source_english.safety_note: Use the assistance platform or a lighter load if the full dip depth cannot stay controlled.

exercises.name: Ski Erg

source_english.description: A ski erg uses a standing hinge and a simultaneous downward pull on the handles to drive the flywheel.
instructions: Stand facing the SkiErg with feet hip-width apart and grasp one handle in each hand.
Reach the arms overhead while keeping the spine long and knees softly bent.
Hinge at the hips and pull both handles down toward the thighs in a strong, smooth stroke.
Allow the arms to rise under control as the hips return to the starting hinge.
form_cues: Finish the pull at the thighs.
Use the hips and lats together.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the handles clear of your body and use a resistance that allows a smooth return.

source_english.description: A ski erg uses a standing hinge and a simultaneous downward pull on the handles to drive the flywheel.
instructions: Stand facing the SkiErg with feet hip-width apart and grasp one handle in each hand.
Reach the arms overhead while keeping the spine long and knees softly bent.
Hinge at the hips and pull both handles down toward the thighs in a strong, smooth stroke.
Allow the arms to rise under control as the hips return to the starting hinge.
form_cues: Finish the pull at the thighs.
Use the hips and lats together.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the handles clear of your body and use a resistance that allows a smooth return.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
